fix.notes: The guard `if LANGUAGES and locale not in LANGUAGES` is intentional: LANGUAGES is populated lazily by init(), so an empty list means 'not yet initialised' — we don't reject in that case. Once init() runs (which happens at app startup), any unrecognised locale is safely dropped. No product decision about locale-switching UX was touched.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

When a user passed an unrecognized locale via the `?locale=` querystring (e.g. `?locale=na`), `check_sql_injection` in `shared_web/localization.py` only validated the value against a character-class regex (`^[a-zA-Z_]+$`). Any string of letters passed through, was stored in the session, and later when Flask-Babel called `Locale.parse()` on it, Babel raised `UnknownLocaleError`, which bubbled up as an unhandled 500.

## What changed

Added a two-line guard in `check_sql_injection` (`shared_web/localization.py:25-26`): after the regex check, if `LANGUAGES` has been populated (i.e. `init()` has run) and the supplied locale is not in that list, the function returns `None` — same as for malformed input. The `if LANGUAGES and ...` guard avoids rejecting all locales before `init()` has had a chance to populate the list.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks)
- `uv run --frozen pytest -x -q -m 'not functional and not perf'` (excluding DB-heavy modules) — 220 passed, 48 deselected. Full suite requires a database; DB-dependent tests in `magic/` and `decksite/` were excluded due to the test environment not having the cards DB initialised, which is an environmental constraint unrelated to this change.

Fixes #6153
fix.pr_title: Reject unrecognized locales to prevent UnknownLocaleError 500s (#6153)

LANGUAGES list is populated at init time from babel.list_translations() but is never consulted when accepting a locale from querystring

triage.fix_sketch: In shared_web/localization.py, add `if locale not in LANGUAGES: return None` inside check_sql_injection after the regex check (line 24). This prevents any unrecognized locale from being stored in session or returned, eliminating the UnknownLocaleError 500. Optionally raise BadRequestException for the abort(400) requirement. The separate item 'do not use querystring for locale' is a product decision about the locale-switching UX and should not be bundled here.
triage.notes: The querystring-locale checkbox (item 1 in the issue) requires a product decision on how users switch language if not via querystring; that is out of scope for this easy-fix. The 500-error fix (item 2) is a 3-line change.
